summary: PYRO-0G is an interactive fire-safety cockpit that makes NASA microgravity combustion research useful for mission planning. It turns records from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Combustion Science repository into a searchable dataset and lets users compare how materials burn across oxygen levels, pressure, airflow, and gravity. A simulator explores crew environments including the ISS, Orion, lunar bases, and pressurized rovers; a transparent Flame Hazard Index ranks conditions; and a “Will it burn?” checker and experiment matrix link results to source evidence. Each record includes a NASA source and evidence quote. Twenty of the 25 records currently pass independent verification checks; the rest are flagged, and missing source values are shown as data gaps rather than guessed. PYRO-0G helps researchers and mission planners explore evidence for safer spacecraft materials while making NASA experiments easier to inspect and reuse.
details:
PYRO-0G combines a data pipeline with an interactive web app. We compiled publicly available NASA PSI Combustion Science investigations, including BASS, BASS-II, Saffire I–III, SAME/SAME-R, FLEX, DAFT, and DAFT-2, along with related NASA Technical Reports Server sources.

Python scripts extract structured fields from source text, including fuel or material, oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity, outcome, and an evidence quote. Claims are checked through an independent verification ladder and human review. Twenty of the 25 records currently pass independent verification; the remaining records are visibly flagged. When a source does not report a measurement, the app shows a data gap instead of estimating a value.

The Simulator Workbench lets users explore crew-environment presets, choose a material, adjust atmospheric conditions, and compare the same sample at 1g and 0g. The Flame Hazard Index uses a visible formula: HI = 100 × (0.35·S + 0.25·O + 0.20·E + 0.20·C). The experiment matrix, hazard cards, and “Will it burn?” checker help users explore the dataset. An evidence inspector links each record to its NASA source and quote, and users can export the data as CSV.

The project is intended to help researchers and mission planners investigate fire safety for spacecraft, stations, lunar bases, and pressurized rovers. It also makes decades of microgravity combustion research easier for the public to explore. We built the pipeline in Python and the static app with JavaScript, Canvas, and SVG; the app is hosted on Vercel.
dataRefs: A Researcher’s Guide to International Space Station Combustion Science (2015)
